detail: Map with open root 'map' and decided children map-reopen, map-stale; spec with stories 1-3; two valid tickets as described. `werk ticket-check tickets --root map --spec spec.md` printed only the summary line '0 failure(s) in all' and exited 0.

Three tickets passed together (exit 0). After deleting ticket 2's touches line, adding 'edit src/loop.ts' to ticket 3's What to build, and setting ticket 1 touches to 'map view, server/routes', output held '02-stale.md: shape: touches: ...', '03-loop.md: no-file-paths: What to build: line 10 names the file path "src/loop.ts"' (line 10 is correct), and '01-reopen.md: touches: touches: "server/routes" reads as a path'. Exit 1.

Four tickets passed together. After removing '## What to build' from ticket 2: '02-stale.md: shape: What to build: the heading "## What to build" is missing', 'no ticket cites the decided card #map-stale', 'no ticket delivers story 3', '04-after.md: blocked_by: ... blocker 2 is not a ticket in the set'. Exit 1.

Output named uncited #map-reopen, 'no ticket delivers story 4', 'story 9 is listed, but the spec has no story 9', 02-two.md and 03-three.md on a blocked_by cycle, 05-five.md 'blocker 8 is not a ticket in the set'; no blocked_by line for 01 or 04. Exit 1.

The first check printed exactly one failure, 'no ticket delivers story 3', and exited 1. The test then edited ticket 2's stories line to 'stories: 3' (standing in for the agent's edit). The rerun printed '0 failure(s)' and exited 0.

Playwright (.werk-heldout/e2e-c/plan-accept.spec.ts on the e2e harness): appended a decided auth subtree to the fixture log and scripted the fake spec writer and ticket writer. Ran `werk plan auth`. The first new board-log event was tier.recorded with tier feature. The Board view showed both tickets (numbered 11 and 12, because the fixture board already uses 1-5). The map nested ghosts #auth-token-ttl and #auth-split-login under #auth with data-proposed=true. Each card view showed its title, why, body and who 'me' (the plan sets who 'me', which the binder reads as the agent). Pressing 'Accept #auth-token-ttl' and then 'Accept #auth-split-login' made each card real, one at a time, with node.accepted events by actor 'you'. A bun test also checked the same facts through `werk show`.

The map already held an accepted card auth-token-ttl, and the spec writer returned slug token-ttl. `werk plan auth` exited 1. The output said 'spec writer answer auth-token-ttl: "auth-token-ttl" is already in the map'. The log still held one node.proposed event for auth-token-ttl, and show printed the original title.

Ticket 01-login.md had no stories line and was the only ticket that cited auth-session. Ticket 02-logout.md was valid. After the plan, the board (board-log fold) held 'logout' and not 'login'. The output held '01-login.md: shape: stories: the header line "stories:" is missing' and 'no ticket cites the decided card #auth-session'.

Ticket a had no What to build heading and failed its own checks. Ticket b was valid. Ticket c had blocked_by 1, 2. The board fold showed blocked=[c] and ready=[b], with a absent. The output said 'blocked 3 c: blocker 1 is not a ticket in the set'.

The first plan put login and logout in ready. The second plan, with only login, appended ticket.archived for logout with the reason 'the current spec of auth no longer needs it', and login stayed in ready. Those parts pass. The restore part fails. No verb or UI control restores an archived ticket: `werk help` lists only `restore` for removed map cards, and the web board has no restore control. `werk restore 2` exited 1 with 'no removed node "2"', and logout stayed archived. Only a later plan that writes the ticket again brings it back. The binder reads this as a missing feature, not a binder error.

The fake builder replies were red, then green. `werk build 7` exited 0 with 'pass 2: green'. The branch held exactly two commits: 'werk build 7: pass 1' and 'werk build 7: pass 2'. The run record had 2 lines. Each line had checks, ms and costUsd (0.1, then 0.2). Line 1 had make check ok=false and line 2 had ok=true.

The check printed about 20,000 'y' characters, then 'TAIL-OF-OUTPUT done.txt is missing', and failed. The second builder prompt named 'make check' and held the tail mark. Its failure text, from 'Last failure' to the end, was 4014 characters. The first prompt held no output and no tail mark; it ends 'Nothing has failed yet.'.

Main got a new tip commit. Then the main checkout got an uncommitted edit to a tracked file and an untracked file. After `werk build 7`, the first parent of the first pass commit was the main tip. `git log -p main..branch` did not contain either local change. The main checkout still had both changes, and git status showed notes.txt as modified.

The builder was always red. `werk build 7` with the default cap exited 1 and printed 'stopped at the retry cap of 5 passes; the branch ... stays'. The branch existed with 5 commits past main. The run record had 5 lines. Each line had green=false, a failed check, ms and costUsd.

The ticket was in the ready column of the board fold before the build. The builder ran red, red, then green. After the build, the board fold (the data that /api/board serves) showed the ticket in building with retries 2. The binder checked the column after the build ended, not live during the build.
